title: Closing a $12k/month agency client: performance-based pricing, benchmarks and culture-fit framing
summary: Iman walks through a live two-call close of an e-commerce client, showing how he pre-frames results and culture fit, sets a performance fee that only kicks in above the client's existing baseline, and uses a break for partners to decide. The closing talk covers why the structure keeps incentives aligned and protects against churn at high billables.

principles.text: Use a cheap first call to stall and gather info when unprepared; then make the offer on a second call.
principles.quote: this initial call is basically me stalling and just getting some preliminary information and then kicking that the can down the road.

principles.text: Pre-frame the sales call with two gates (results and culture fit) so prospects qualify themselves without cringe.
principles.quote: there's two things that need to be a green light. First of all, results front.

principles.text: Ask what success looks like and pin down numbers (revenue, spend, ROAS) to align expectations before pricing.
principles.quote: if you want to do it kind of maintaining your margins as is, uh you know, then it's definitely a conversation we can entertain.

principles.text: Set the performance fee to start only above the client's existing baseline, so you never take credit for what they already do.
principles.quote: I actually set a benchmark of what they're already accomplishing, so we actually don't, uh, in terms of our performance fee, it only kicks in at a certain boundary.

principles.text: Keep the base retainer low and make most pay performance-based, so incentives are aligned and the deal is a no-brainer.
principles.quote: we don't take a percentage of ad spend. We don't take a percentage of revenue. We take a percentage of what we're making you after ads on the campaigns.

principles.text: Use a 6-month minimum then rolling monthly, since high billables without a baseline structure invite churn.
principles.quote: it's a 6-month minimum. That's standard with us, so we we don't take clients on for anything less than that, um, these days.
